newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear in talks ahead of contract expiry.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear in talks ahead of contract expiry.

text.p: Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co said Thursday it was in talks with the United Steelworkers union ahead of the Saturday midnight EDT expiration of the contract covering 12,000 of the tiremaker's 91,000 workers.
Both sides agreed to a news blackout when negotiations on a new three-year contract began about two months ago. Talks continued this week in neutral territory at a Cincinnati hotel.
Goodyear, the largest U.S. tiremaker with about 16 percent of the market, is the union's target in pattern bargaining with the industry, United Steelworkers of America spokesman Curt Brown said.

Besides the traditional issues of wages and benefits, one issue likely to be under discussion was the union's desire to have the various contracts covering Goodyear's 20,000 union workers expire at the same time.
"We're going to either have an agreement, continue the current contract if we're close, or we'll strike," Brown said.
Neither the union nor Goodyear spokesman Fred Haymond would offer any clues about progress in the negotiations.
Saul Ludwig, an analyst at McDonald and Co, said, "I would say congratulations to them for keeping the negotiations quiet." Ludwig has a "buy" rating on Goodyear's stock.
"The questions are: Will there be a strike? If so, how many plants? How many workers? Every company would have a contingency plan but it's futile to speculate," he said.
The 12,000 union employees covered by the expiring master contract work at nine of the global tire maker's 45 U.S. facilities.
One sore point for Goodyear's U.S. workers, which they have in common with automotive and other workers, is the exporting of jobs to countries where labor costs are cheaper.

The Steelworkers' Brown said the union was irritated by a statement made at the company's annual meeting this week by Goodyear chairman Samir Gibara that some 200 jobs would move to Chile from Akron as the company shifted production of bias-ply racing tires there.
Although pattern bargaining was in effect, union workers at Goodyear's largest competitor, Bridgestone Corp, have a contract that extends for another three years.

That contract for Bridgestone/Firestone workers grew out of a lengthy and bitter 1994 strike during which the company used replacement workers and imported tires. The long strike sapped the United Rubber Workers' strike fund, and the union subsequently joined the steelworkers to form a 740,000-member union.
Goodyear is the largest single employer of the union's membership, Brown said.
